He recommends users explicitly instruct chatbots to cite sources and verify any provided links before accepting factual claims.
items.title: Jared Smith warns users to verify AI sources after Google cited broken links

key_points: Fervo Energy and Google signed a landmark agreement to supply nearly 400 megawatts of geothermal power from Utah.
The deal supports the second phase of Fervo's Cape Station project, which is expected to begin operations in about two years.
Google intends to use the electricity for a potential data center in the state.
Fervo shares rose 15% following the announcement of the partnership.
items.summary: Fervo Energy and Google signed a landmark agreement to supply nearly 400 megawatts of geothermal power from Utah. The deal supports the second phase of Fervo's Cape Station project, which is expected to begin operations in about two years. Google intends to use the electricity for a potential data center in the state. Fervo shares rose 15% following the announcement of the partnership.
items.title: Fervo Energy signs largest next-gen geothermal deal with Google

key_points: Tesla stopped supplying Solar Roof tiles in August, notifying installers it would ship only conventional panels.
Certified contractors invested heavily in training and tooling for a product that achieved only about 3,000 total installations over seven years.
Installers fear long-term warranty and parts availability issues despite Tesla's promise to support existing systems.
The article concludes that Tesla successfully exited the low-margin installation business while partners remain stuck with the costs.
items.summary: Tesla abruptly ended its Solar Roof program in August, shifting exclusively to conventional solar panels and leaving certified third-party contractors to absorb the financial fallout. Over seven years, the company installed only about 3,000 systems, failing to meet Elon Musk's earlier targets for weekly installations. Contractors report spending hundreds of thousands of dollars on specialized training and tooling that is now largely useless. While Tesla promises to honor existing warranties, installers express skepticism regarding long-term parts availability and service complexity for the discontinued product. The article notes that Tesla offloaded the labor-intensive installation business to partners before exiting, leaving them with stranded investments and abandoned projects.
items.title: Tesla discontinues Solar Roof, leaving third-party installers with significant financial losses

key_points: The EU is replacing dependence on Russian fossil fuels with reliance on Chinese clean energy components.
Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra warned that reducing Chinese dependence is urgent to avoid higher future costs.
The European Court of Auditors reported that import diversification efforts have not produced tangible results.
A Loom report noted China supplied 98% of European solar panels and 88% of lithium-ion battery imports in 2024.
items.summary: The European Union faces a critical challenge as its green energy transition creates heavy reliance on China for solar panels, wind turbines, and critical minerals. EU Climate Action Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra stated that building domestic capacity is necessary despite short-term costs, warning that delays will increase long-term expenses. A report by the European Court of Auditors found that current efforts to diversify imports are failing due to bottlenecks in domestic production and recycling. Additionally, a strategy center report by Loom highlighted that China supplied 98% of European solar panels and 88% of lithium-ion battery imports in 2024. Analysts caution that without significant de-risking of clean technology manufacturing, the EU's economic security and AI ambitions could be undermined by continued dependence on Chinese batteries and infrastructure.
items.title: EU Struggles to Reduce Dependence on China for Clean Energy

key_points: Solar power is growing rapidly in emerging markets due to low costs and energy security needs.
Europe is experiencing a slowdown because of grid congestion and a lack of storage capacity.
Romania achieved a 45 percent increase in solar installations in 2025 by deploying storage early.
Countries like Pakistan and Kenya are adopting rooftop solar-plus-battery systems faster than the United States.
items.summary: Solar power adoption is accelerating globally, driven by cheap Chinese panels and energy security needs. While Europe faces grid congestion and storage shortages, emerging economies are leading the transition. Romania stands out for integrating storage early, achieving a 45 percent increase in solar installations in 2025. Poorer nations like Pakistan, Brazil, and Kenya are rapidly deploying rooftop solar-plus-battery systems to bypass unreliable infrastructure. The Economist notes that countries must now balance generation with storage. CNN reports that Pakistan has become a major market for these systems. Oilprice.com states that solar is now the cheapest energy source, offering autonomy for smaller economies.
items.title: Emerging Markets Lead Solar Growth While Europe Struggles With Grid Limits

key_points: Montana crews are using strategic firing to contain the Bobcat Lakes and Sand Creek wildfires.
The U.S. Forest Service states this tactic removes fuel to create a safer barrier for firefighters.
Officials confirmed that acres burned during these operations are included in the total reported acreage.
Fire managers rely on indirect tactics more often due to longer fire seasons and heavier fuel loads.
items.summary: Montana firefighters are intentionally burning vegetation to contain the Bobcat Lakes and Sand Creek wildfires. The U.S. Forest Service describes this tactic as an indirect firefighting method used when direct attack is too dangerous. Mariah Leuschen-Lonergan, a fire communications lead, explained that burning removes fuel before the main fire reaches it, creating a safer working area and protecting private property. Officials confirmed that acres burned during these operations are included in the total reported acreage of 45,561 acres. Crews carefully monitor weather conditions, including wind speed and fuel moisture, before approving any firing operation. Leuschen-Lonergan noted that increasing fire seasons and heavier fuel loads are making direct attacks harder, leading to greater reliance on these indirect suppression methods.
items.title: Montana firefighters use strategic burning to contain two wildfires

key_points: Governor Mikie Sherrill signed the Garden State Balcony Solar Act to legalize plug-in solar systems.
The law permits systems up to 1,200 watts on balconies or patios without permits or utility approval.
Landlords cannot ban qualifying systems if tenants pay the electric bill, though they may set reasonable placement rules.
The legislation takes effect on March 1, 2027.
items.summary: Governor Mikie Sherrill signed the Garden State Balcony Solar Act, legalizing small solar systems that plug into standard wall outlets. The law allows systems up to 1,200 watts on balconies or patios without permits or utility approval. Landlords cannot ban these systems if tenants pay the electric bill, though they can set reasonable placement rules. Doug O'Malley of Environment New Jersey stated the technology helps residents save money and participate in clean energy. The legislation takes effect on March 1, 2027.
items.title: New Jersey legalizes plug-in solar panels for renters and homeowners

key_points: Encore Renewable Energy installed a 2.25-MW solar array on a closed landfill in Derry, New Hampshire.
The project is projected to save Derry taxpayers an estimated $4 million in electricity costs over 25 years.
Encore founder Chad Farrell described the landfill as an untapped resource offering cleared land with good sun exposure.
The Derry NetZero Task Force spent six years developing the plan before selecting Encore from seven firms in 2021.
Task force chair Jeff Moulton said the project will provide 100% of the town's electricity needs for the next 25 years.
items.summary: Encore Renewable Energy has activated a 2.25-MW solar project atop a capped landfill in Derry, New Hampshire. The facility is expected to save taxpayers approximately $4 million over 25 years. Encore founder Chad Farrell noted the site offers cleared land with sufficient sun exposure and proximity to electrical infrastructure. The Derry NetZero Task Force developed the plan over six years, leading to Encore's selection from seven firms in 2021. Jeff Moulton, task force chair, stated the project will provide 100% of the town's electricity needs for the next 25 years.
items.title: Encore Renewable Energy installs 2.25-MW solar array on Derry landfill

key_points: California initiated legal action against the Trump administration and Golden State Wind following the cancellation of an offshore wind lease.
The lawsuit challenges a federal agreement requiring Golden State Wind to receive $120m while investing an equivalent amount in fossil fuel projects outside California.
State officials argue the cancellation undermines commitments to generate 25 GW of offshore wind power by 2045 and threatens over 174,750 jobs.
Attorney General Rob Bonta and the California Energy Commission have asked the court to halt the agreement and restore the lease.
items.summary: California has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration and Golden State Wind regarding the cancellation of an offshore wind project. The state challenges a federal agreement that would reimburse Golden State Wind $120m in exchange for investing in out-of-state fossil fuels. Attorney General Rob Bonta and the California Energy Commission argue the termination undermines climate goals and threatens over 174,750 jobs. They seek to halt the deal and restore the lease.
items.title: California sues Trump administration over cancelled offshore wind project buyout

key_points: The Department of Agriculture and Department of Energy are working on a joint plan to protect agricultural land from excessive solar development.
Agriculture Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel Jr. proposed geofencing around 3 million hectares of flat agricultural land to preserve rice production areas.
The two agencies target signing a memorandum of agreement by October 2026 to formalize their cooperation on land use and energy planning.
Officials are exploring arrangements to reduce electricity costs for farmers and fisherfolk through direct access to renewable energy suppliers.
items.summary: The Department of Agriculture and Department of Energy are developing a joint strategy to protect agricultural land while expanding renewable energy. Agriculture Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel Jr. proposed geofencing approximately 3 million hectares of flat farmland to prevent excessive solar development. The agencies aim to sign a memorandum of agreement by October 2026 to formalize this cooperation. Officials are also exploring frameworks to reduce electricity costs for farmers and fisherfolk through direct renewable energy access.
items.title: Philippines DA and DOE plan geofencing to shield farmland from solar projects

key_points: The Australian Energy Market Commission recommended that large data centers must bring their own clean, firmed energy and pay full connection costs.
McDermott International and ULC-Energy signed an agreement to support Rolls-Royce small modular reactor projects in the Netherlands.
Baker Hughes received a 1.3-GW order for industrial gas turbines from Dynamis Power Solutions to support data centers and oil and gas sectors.
Origis Energy announced that its Rockhound Solar complex in Texas has reached nearly 1 GW of operating capacity.
TotalEnergies and partners launched the Hydra project in South Africa, the largest hybrid renewable energy project on the continent.
items.summary: The Australian Energy Market Commission urged ministers to require large data centers to generate their own clean, firm power and pay full network costs. Legislation targeting early 2027 introduction aims to make facilities net-generators rather than net-users. McDermott International signed a cooperation agreement with ULC-Energy to develop Rolls-Royce small modular reactors in the Netherlands. Baker Hughes announced a 1.3-GW gas turbine order from Dynamis Power Solutions for data centers and oil and gas applications. Origis Energy reached a 1-GW milestone at its Rockhound Solar complex in Texas, with plans to exceed 2 GW by 2029. key_points: Holtec International announced that fuel loading has commenced at the Palisades nuclear plant.
Chief Nuclear Officer Fadi Diya described the milestone as a reflection of the team's tremendous effort.
The facility was transferred to Holtec in 2021 for decommissioning before a restart plan was initiated.
Extensive maintenance and upgrades were completed to ensure reliability.
Holtec notified regulators of plans to seek a license extension to 2051 and deploy small modular reactors at the site.
items.summary: Holtec International announced that fuel loading has commenced at the Palisades nuclear plant. Chief Nuclear Officer Fadi Diya described the milestone as a reflection of the team's tremendous effort. The facility, originally operated by Entergy, was transferred to Holtec in 2021 for decommissioning before a restart plan was initiated. items.title: Holtec International begins fuel loading for Palisades nuclear restart

key_points: Henri Francois argues federal coal orders contradict nuclear regulatory delays.
The Department of Energy issued over 40 emergency orders since May 2025.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission took more than a year to recommend TVA reactor approval.
Francois claims coal plants run on afternoon orders while reactors wait for meetings.
items.summary: Henri Francois argues that federal emergency orders keeping coal plants open contradict nuclear regulatory timelines. The author notes the Department of Energy issued over 40 emergency orders since May 2025 to hold coal generation, including Centralia in Washington. Meanwhile, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission took more than a year to recommend approval for a Tennessee Valley Authority small modular reactor. Francois states that coal plants can be ordered to run in an afternoon while reactors wait for meetings. He claims the Department of Energy uses a forecast ERCOT admits is too high to justify keeping coal units active. The author concludes that applying emergency authority to inflated data while slowing nuclear progress creates an unfair energy policy.
items.title: Author argues coal orders and nuclear delays show energy planning asymmetry

The company reports models suggesting annual output could rise by 10% to 30% by reducing cloud reflectivity.
Meteoric plans to deploy electric drones at altitudes between 1 km and 5 km starting in 2027.
The firm estimates potential revenue gains of $5,000 to $28,000 per MW and aims to test storm intervention by late 2028.
items.summary: US startup Meteoric Technologies is developing a chemical-free drone system to modify cloud optical properties and increase solar power generation. Meteoric plans to deploy electric drones at altitudes between 1 km and 5 km starting in 2027. items.title: Meteoric Technologies develops drone fleet to modify clouds and boost solar output

The Solar Energy Association of Ukraine (ASEU) reports a 50 MW auction with a maximum bid of €0.08/kWh and a 100 MW solar-plus-storage auction capped at €0.12/kWh.
Participation in the storage auction requires systems to be at least 80% of installed capacity.
The auctions cover multiple regions but exclude areas of active hostilities.
items.summary: Ukraine's state-owned JSC Guaranteed Buyer will run two solar auctions on September 25 offering a combined 150 MW. The Solar Energy Association of Ukraine (ASEU) reports a 50 MW auction with a maximum bid of €0.08/kWh and a 100 MW solar-plus-storage auction capped at €0.12/kWh. Ukraine deployed around 1.5 GW of solar in 2025, bringing cumulative capacity to over 8.5 GW.
items.title: Ukraine auctions 150 MW of solar power in two upcoming events

key_points: A new report from the NGO Shipbreaking Platform and T&E states that the vast majority of EU-owned and EU-flagged ships are dismantled in South Asia despite sufficient domestic recycling capacity.
Between 2019 and 2025, only 22% of these vessels were recycled in EU facilities, representing just 5% of total tonnage.
Benedetta Mantoan, Policy Manager at the NGO Shipbreaking Platform, described this trend as a failure of EU industrial strategy that exports valuable steel.
The study highlights that beaching in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh exposes workers to dangerous conditions and contaminates the environment.
items.summary: A new report from the NGO Shipbreaking Platform and T&E states that the vast majority of EU-owned and EU-flagged ships are dismantled in South Asia despite sufficient domestic recycling capacity. Between 2019 and 2025, only 22% of these vessels were recycled in EU facilities, representing just 5% of total tonnage. Benedetta Mantoan, Policy Manager at the NGO Shipbreaking Platform, described this trend as a failure of EU industrial strategy that exports valuable steel. The study highlights that beaching in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh exposes workers to dangerous conditions and contaminates the environment. Benedetta Mantoan noted that up to 95% of a ship's weight can be recycled as high-quality scrap steel. The report argues that persisting policy gaps prevent recycling from aligning with the Union's strategic plans. T&E emphasized that secondary steel production via electric arc furnaces is a key pathway to decarbonise the sector.
items.title: New Study Confirms Most EU Ships Are Scrapped in South Asia

key_points: Ford is converting its Louisville Assembly Plant into a fully electric vehicle facility to support its new Fathom midsize truck.
The company emptied the site in February 2026 for a $2 billion overhaul to install a new Universal EV Production System.
Ford aims to begin building Fathom prototypes with production parts in the first quarter of 2027, with customer deliveries starting later that year.
Chief manufacturing officer Bryce Currie stated the new method reduces reaching over the fender by 84% and shortens wiring harnesses.
items.summary: Ford is converting its Louisville Assembly Plant into a fully electric vehicle facility to support its new Fathom midsize truck. The company emptied the site in February 2026 for a $2 billion overhaul to install a new Universal EV Production System. Ford aims to begin building Fathom prototypes with production parts in the first quarter of 2027, with customer deliveries starting later that year. Chief manufacturing officer Bryce Currie stated the new method reduces reaching over the fender by 84% and shortens wiring harnesses. The design draws inspiration from Chinese automakers and utilizes large unicastings to simplify assembly. Ford plans to increase assembly density and improve ergonomics for operators on the production line.
items.title: Ford transforms Louisville plant for 2027 Fathom EV production

key_points: A source indicated that EU antitrust regulators are monitoring Oracle's licensing practices.
The European Commission is requesting information from third parties regarding the issue.
A commission spokesperson confirmed there is no formal investigation into any company at this stage.
The situation mirrors a July settlement involving SAP that avoided a potential fine.
items.summary: A person familiar with the matter stated that EU antitrust regulators are investigating Oracle's licensing practices. The European Commission is seeking information from third parties to determine if a formal case should be opened. A spokesperson noted there is currently no formal investigation into any specific company. This scrutiny follows a July settlement involving rival firm SAP regarding similar anticompetitive concerns.
items.title: EU antitrust regulators examine Oracle licensing practices amid SAP precedent

Internal testing indicates Astra is significantly more capable than the current public model, GPT-5.6 Sol.

items.summary: OpenAI officials stated that their upcoming model, Astra, requires additional safety measures due to its advanced capabilities. key_points: Standard checklists often miss specific drawers containing small, sharp, or swallowable items.
Cords present dual strangulation and pulling hazards that outlet-focused childproofing does not address.
Less frequently used rooms like guest bedrooms often get baby-proofed last despite being explored by mobile babies.
Furniture tip-over risk depends on stability and climbing behavior rather than height alone.
Baby-proofing reduces risk but does not eliminate the need for active supervision.
items.summary: The article identifies eight specific baby-proofing gaps that standard checklists often ignore. It notes that parents frequently overlook specific drawers containing small hazards and fail to audit cords for strangulation risks. The text also highlights that less-used rooms like guest bedrooms often get missed and that furniture stability matters more than height alone. Additionally, it warns against assuming doorstops are safe and emphasizes that baby-proofing reduces risk but does not replace active supervision. Finally, the article advises that safety measures must be reassessed as a baby's skills develop. Each point explains why the hazard is missed and offers a practical adjustment for parents.
items.title: Parents overlook eight baby-proofing hazards standard checklists miss

key_points: Dell posted record second-quarter revenue of $46.97 billion, beating analyst expectations.
The company raised its full-year revenue guidance by $25 billion to approximately $192 billion.
AI-optimized server sales are projected to reach $74 billion for the fiscal year.
Dell reported a backlog of $95 billion in AI servers at the end of the quarter.
items.summary: Dell Technologies reported record second-quarter revenue of $46.97 billion, prompting a $25 billion increase in its full-year revenue outlook to approximately $192 billion. The company attributes this growth to surging demand for AI-optimized servers, which contributed $74 billion annually. Dell's stock rose about 8% in extended trading following the announcement. CFO David Kennedy stated that the company's strengths drove growth and profitability throughout the quarter.
items.title: Dell raises full-year revenue outlook by $25 billion due to AI server demand

The deal is designed to address shared security threats between the two nations.
Rising tensions between Greece and Turkiye provide context for the strengthened military partnership.
items.summary: Israel and Greece have signed a $3.5 billion weapons agreement for the Achilles Shield air defence system. The deal aims to counter common threats as tensions rise between Greece and Turkiye. Regional experts discuss the implications of this strengthened alliance on the broader geopolitical landscape.
items.title: Israel and Greece sign $3.5bn defence deal amid regional tensions

key_points: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney demanded the US take a serious approach to resolve trade disputes.
The US imposed 50 percent tariffs on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods following failed negotiations.
Canada pledged retaliatory tariffs on US goods worth the same dollar amount starting September 8.
Carney accused the Trump administration of attempting to limit Canada's ability to strike free trade deals with other countries.
items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney criticized the United States for a flippant approach to ongoing trade tensions. Carney stated that negotiations can only proceed once Washington adopts a more serious stance. The dispute escalated after President Donald Trump imposed 50 percent tariffs on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods in August. Canada pledged retaliatory tariffs on US goods starting September 8. Carney accused the Trump administration of seeking to limit Canada's trade autonomy and alter laws protecting French language and culture. While Trump has called Canada one of the worst countries to deal with, Carney emphasized Canada's sovereignty and refusal to accept asymmetrical terms. US officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have also made disparaging remarks about Canada.
items.title: Canada's Carney demands US seriousness to resolve trade dispute

key_points: Bandhan Life CEO Satishwar B. states that knee surgery alone does not automatically result in term insurance rejection or higher premiums.
Insurers evaluate the nature of the injury, recovery status, and current mobility to determine policy terms and premium rates.
Applicants are required to disclose accidents and provide comprehensive medical records for underwriting assessment.
Individuals who have fully recovered and maintain normal daily mobility face better chances of policy approval with minimal premium impact.
Bandhan Life recommends considering disability riders for potential condition recurrence, subject to specific product eligibility and exclusions.
items.summary: Satishwar B., MD and CEO of Bandhan Life, states that a past accident or knee surgery does not automatically lead to term insurance rejection or higher premiums. Insurers assess recovery status, current mobility, and the likelihood of future complications before deciding policy terms. Applicants must disclose the accident and provide complete medical records, including hospitalization details and doctor assessments. If an applicant has fully recovered and can perform daily activities normally, approval chances are generally better with little impact on the premium. For those worried about condition recurrence, Bandhan Life suggests exploring disability riders, though coverage depends on specific product terms and medical history. The company advises against postponing insurance applications due to surgery, emphasizing that individual medical conditions and underwriting assessments determine the final outcome.
items.title: Bandhan Life CEO says past knee surgery does not automatically raise term insurance premiums

key_points: Meta disabled cameras on thousands of smart glasses after detecting tampering with the camera-indicating LED light.
The company rolled out an update to identify covered or destroyed lights following reports of non-consensual recording.
Alex Himel, Meta's vice president of wearables, stated that less than one tenth of a percent of sold glasses have been tampered with.
Meta is also launching a marketing campaign to raise public awareness about recording indicators.
items.summary: Meta disabled cameras on thousands of smart glasses after detecting tampering with the camera-indicating LED light. The company rolled out an update to identify covered or destroyed lights following reports of non-consensual recording. Alex Himel, Meta's vice president of wearables, stated that less than one tenth of a percent of sold glasses have been tampered with. Meta is also launching a marketing campaign to raise public awareness about recording indicators. Additionally, the company is donating 130,000 glasses to legally blind US veterans and seeking classification as an assistive device.
items.title: Meta disables cameras on thousands of tampered smart glasses

key_points: Democratizations cause large negative impacts on asset valuations due to increased redistribution risk.
Risk premia rise substantially before and during democratizations, comparable to financial crises.
A shift in Catholic church doctrine supports the causal link between democratization and higher risk.
Reductions in inequality and increased taxes explain approximately half of the observed results.
items.summary: Max Miller reports that democratizations significantly raise asset risk premia and increase redistribution across 90 countries over 200 years. The study finds that successful transitions expand the public sector, reduce inequality, and raise the labor share of income. A shift in Catholic church doctrine provided causal evidence linking democratization to higher risk. Miller's model explains these effects through inequality reductions, increased taxes, and greater economic competition.
items.title: Democratizations Increase Asset Risk Premia and Boost Redistribution

These animals are seeking food due to widespread shortages in their natural habitats.
The situation has prompted increased concern about human-wildlife conflicts in the region.
items.summary: Experts report that drought conditions across the US west are causing record numbers of bears to wander into human homes and shops. items.title: Experts say drought drives record numbers of hungry bears into US homes

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly demanded Japan cut spending and raise interest rates to stabilize its currency.
Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh stated that interest rate increases are expected to address inflationary pressures.
The authors warn that global bond market turmoil could prevent Burnham's industrial strategy from succeeding.
items.summary: The Guardian editorial argues that global bond market turmoil linked to Gulf inflation pressures UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's economic strategy. The authors report that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has demanded Japan reduce spending and raise rates to prevent currency instability. Kevin Warsh, the Federal Reserve chair, indicated interest rate hikes are expected in response to inflation. The editorial warns that similar fiscal constraints could derail Burnham's reindustrialisation agenda before it begins.
items.title: Global bond shock complicates Andy Burnham's UK industrial plans

key_points: Delhi Traffic Police announced major traffic diversions for a BRICS motorcade rehearsal on September 2.
Regulated movement will occur between 10 am and 3 pm across more than 35 roads in the capital.
Emergency and essential-service vehicles will receive priority passage during the event.
Metro services will remain operational while road-based feeder and bus services may face diversions.
items.summary: Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory warning commuters of significant traffic diversions on September 2 for a BRICS Leaders' Summit motorcade rehearsal. Restrictions will apply between 10 am and 3 pm across more than 35 roads and 22 diversion points. Emergency vehicles will receive priority passage while the public is urged to use public transport. Metro services will remain operational, though road-based feeder buses may face delays.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police announces major road diversions for BRICS Summit 2026 rehearsal

key_points: Bill Cohan's new 673-page biography offers a narrative that contrasts with The New York Times reporting on Leon Black.
Cohan views his book as a rebuttal to what he describes as a 'Leon jihad' by journalists including The Times.
Times journalists David Enrich and Matt Goldstein have criticized Cohan's depiction of them in the book.
The conflict focuses on differing interpretations of Black's role regarding Jeffrey Epstein and financial payments.

items.title: Bill Cohan's new book challenges New York Times reporting on Leon Black

MGM Investment Properties Inc. filed a lawsuit against the owner seeking payment for kitchen equipment.
Spartan Capital is the largest unsecured creditor, owed over $178,000, according to the Chapter 11 petition.
items.summary: Asani Restaurant Group LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Florida on Aug. 31, listing over $75,000 in assets and over $407,000 in debts. MGM Investment Properties Inc. filed a lawsuit against the owner on Jan. 8, 2026, seeking payment for kitchen equipment. Ongoing conflict in Iran has made the Fed's job of controlling price growth extremely difficult.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum prices fall as inflation fears persist

key_points: The authors report that maintenance currently removes roughly one-third of the 48 nuclear-powered attack submarines from operational readiness.
Deployment cycles and geographic distance limit the number of boats available for a specific theater at any given time.
Weapon magazines are finite and require time-consuming replenishment far from the combat zone.
Lost submarines cannot be replaced on a wartime timescale, creating a structural vulnerability.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first 70 percent of this page.
items.summary: A new analysis argues that the United States may overestimate its submarine combat power in a conflict with China. The authors report that nominal inventory numbers do not reflect deployable strength or sustainable combat power. The text states that maintenance currently removes roughly one-third of the 48 nuclear-powered attack submarines from operational readiness. Deployment cycles further limit the number of boats available for a specific theater at any given time. Geographic distance and mission allocation requirements reduce the force that can be concentrated against a particular enemy. The authors note that weapon magazines are finite and require time-consuming replenishment far from the combat zone. Finally, the analysis highlights that lost submarines cannot be replaced on a wartime timescale, creating a structural vulnerability. The Congressional Budget Office reported that Virginia-class production averages only 1.1 submarines per year. The text concludes that while American submarines are capable, their strategic utility depends on complex logistical and operational constraints.
items.title: Analysis questions if U.S. submarines can defeat China in war

key_points: Google Maps changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users to match the US government's Geographic Names Information System.
Apple Maps and MapQuest continue to display the lake as Lake Ontario, with MapQuest publicly rejecting the US government's renaming order.
MapQuest has surged to the top of the US App Store download charts following its decision to defy the renaming.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford responded to the controversy by installing a large sign stating 'Lake Ontario now and always'.
items.summary: Google Maps now displays Lake Ontario as Lake America for users in the United States, aligning with the US government's Geographic Names Information System. Canadians and users elsewhere continue to see the original name or both. Apple Maps and MapQuest retain the name Lake Ontario, with MapQuest publicly rejecting the change and surging in US App Store downloads. The dispute occurs amid strained US-Canada relations as Donald Trump promotes the new name. Ontario Premier Doug Ford responded by displaying a sign reading 'Lake Ontario now and always.'
items.title: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users

key_points: Coles and NSW Police arrested a man for tampering with Apple gift cards in Sydney supermarkets.
Police seized 47 iTunes gift cards from the suspect's home, valuing the total at over $10,000.
The man was convicted in July 2025 and sentenced to 15 months in prison suspended for two years.
Experts warn that national coordination is needed to tackle the volume of this crime effectively.
items.summary: Coles and NSW Police successfully busted a man involved in an Apple gift card tampering scam. The supermarket's fraud team captured the suspect on CCTV while he returned tampered cards to supermarket racks. Police covertly tracked the 32-year-old man and searched his home, seizing 47 iTunes gift cards worth between $100 and $500. He was charged with dishonestly obtaining financial advantage and dealing with proceeds of crime. The man was convicted in July 2025 and received a 15-month suspended prison sentence. Coles stated that gift card fraud is an evolving challenge requiring cooperation across retailers and law enforcement. An ABC investigation linked the issue to a wider global scam involving money laundering. Private investigator Ken Gamble noted that joining the dots nationally remains difficult as agencies like the AFP and AUSTRAC stated it was not their primary domain.
items.title: Coles and NSW Police convict man for Apple gift card tampering

key_points: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged G20 nations to use tariffs to protect their industries from cheap imports.
Bessent warned that Chinese goods could flood markets without protective measures from other countries.
The Tax Foundation found U.S. tariffs raised retail prices of imported goods by roughly 7% in 2025.
Bessent stated global debt reached a record $353 trillion while discussing trade with China.
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters that G20 countries should adopt tariffs to shield their industries from cheap imports. He warned that Chinese goods could flood markets without such measures. The Tax Foundation noted U.S. tariffs raised consumer prices by roughly 7% in 2025. Bessent also discussed de-risking trade with China while noting global debt reached $353 trillion.
items.title: Bessent urges G20 nations to use tariffs against cheap imports

key_points: Leon Collins confirmed the detection of Panama disease TR4 on an 11th Queensland banana farm.
The fungus targets Cavendish varieties, which make up more than 97 per cent of fruit produced in Australia.
Researchers are developing resistant varieties through genetic modification and crossbreeding, with some lines expected by 2028.
Current resistant varieties often suffer yield penalties ranging from 60 to 90 per cent compared to industry standards.
Strict biosecurity measures in the Tully region have contained the disease to that district so far.
items.summary: Leon Collins, chair of the Australian Banana Growers' Council, confirmed that Panama disease tropical race 4 has now infected an 11th banana farm south of Cairns. The soil-borne fungus cannot be eradicated and poses a severe threat to Cavendish bananas, which account for over 97 per cent of Australian production. Researchers are developing resistant varieties using both genetic modification and traditional crossbreeding. In 2024, QUT received approval to commercialise the world's first GM banana, QCAV-4, though consumer acceptance remains uncertain. Other projects aim to release resistant lines by 2028, but current options often suffer yield penalties of 60 to 90 per cent. Strict biosecurity measures in the Tully region have so far contained the disease's spread.
items.title: Panama disease TR4 reaches 11th Queensland farm as breeders seek resistant Cavendish varieties

State media reported a strike near Sirik killed four people and wounded 50.
The IRGC stated retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US bases have begun.
President Trump warned Iran would face harder strikes if it retaliated further.
items.summary: US Central Command announced American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, accusing the IRGC of recent attacks on shipping and service members. State media reported a strike near Sirik killed four people and wounded 50 at a wedding. The IRGC stated retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US bases have begun. President Trump warned Iran would face harder strikes if it retaliated further.
items.title: US resumes strikes on Iran after IRGC attacks shipping and personnel

Burnham promised to kick-start the economy and ease the cost of living.
He outlined a plan for a radical redistribution of power from London to Britain's regions.
Wars in Europe and the Middle East are currently weighing on his economic promises.
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham made his first appearance in the House of Commons on Tuesday. He outlined plans to restart the economy and redistribute power from London to regions. Wars in Europe and the Middle East currently weigh on his economic promises. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen spoke with Dr Martin Farr about the situation.
items.title: Andy Burnham addresses House of Commons on economy and regional power

One judge considered altering a ruling to protect their family from vitriol.

items.title: Federal judges install panic buttons and hire security amid rising threats

The Monterey County Sheriff's Office stated the infant had signs of traumatic injury and the girl is charged with murder.
Authorities believe the father is hiding the teen while he faces multiple sex crime charges.
Sheriff Tina Nieto called for the father to turn himself in and noted the investigation utilized automated license plate readers.

items.title: Police seek 14-year-old girl and father after newborn found dead

The challenge aims to identify innovative technology-enabled solutions created within G20 member states to boost financial understanding.
Bessent promoted the Trump Accounts initiative, noting that approximately 7 million infants are signed up, with 86% from households earning under $200,000 annually.
Critics contend that financial crises result from policy decisions affecting disposable income rather than a lack of financial knowledge.
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced US support for the Financial Literacy Solutions Sprint at a G20 ministers meeting. The contest will select winners from innovative technology solutions developed within G20 member states to improve financial understanding. Bessent also highlighted the Trump Accounts initiative, which deposits $1,000 into investment accounts for infants born during Trump's second term. Critics argue that financial struggles stem from a lack of disposable income rather than ignorance, citing recent survey data showing widespread dissatisfaction with economic conditions.
items.title: Scott Bessent promotes financial literacy contest and Trump-era investment plan at G20

The authors suggest that engaging these groups fosters ownership and empowers communities.
The text notes that current efforts remain fragmented in Southeast Asia despite global restoration initiatives.
items.summary: The authors of a new op-ed argue that integrating Indigenous and local community knowledge into seed propagation strengthens forest restoration outcomes. They state that these communities are indispensable partners due to their familiarity with local species and ecological rhythms. The commentary highlights that focusing on seed quality rather than planting numbers is essential for long-term resilience. Evidence from Indonesia shows local communities developed four propagation techniques to produce tens of thousands of seedlings. The authors suggest that engaging these groups fosters ownership and empowers communities. They recommend incorporating traditional ecological knowledge into technical designs and providing sustainable finance models. The text notes that current efforts remain fragmented in Southeast Asia despite global restoration initiatives.
items.title: Indigenous knowledge improves forest restoration seed production in Southeast Asia

Vance characterized El-Sayed as a threat to common citizenship and American unity.
El-Sayed defended his past comments on a synagogue attack while criticizing Vance's family remarks.
Vance called on Michigan voters to reject El-Sayed and support Republican nominee Mike Rogers.
items.summary: Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed responded to Vice President JD Vance's attacks by defining evil as policies that harm working people. Vance described El-Sayed as representative of terrible evil during a speech in Michigan. El-Sayed accused the vice president of using dog whistles regarding Islamophobia and ethnic division. The exchange also involved comments about Vance's family and El-Sayed's previous remarks on a synagogue attack. Vance urged voters to reject El-Sayed, while El-Sayed called his opponents sock puppets. Both candidates are campaigning for the November election in Michigan.
items.title: Abdul El-Sayed accuses JD Vance of evil rhetoric and dog whistles

key_points: The Starmus Festival board established the Jane Goodall Earth Medal to honor the late conservation icon.
Christiana Figueres was chosen as the inaugural recipient for her relentless advocacy similar to Goodall's spirit.
Festival co-founders Brian May and Peter Gabriel inspired the creation of the medal through their advisory board.
Guests argue that social media algorithms prioritizing engagement over truth contribute to a post-truth era.
Experts suggest regulating tech companies and enhancing education are vital solutions to combat misinformation.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first 50 percent of this page.
items.summary: The Starmus Festival board created the Jane Goodall Earth Medal to honor the late conservationist, with former UN climate chief Christiana Figueres selected as the inaugural recipient. Festival co-founder Garik Israelian explained that advisory members Brian May and Peter Gabriel inspired the award, which aims to celebrate Goodall's legacy of uncompromising advocacy. Figueres expressed deep gratitude, describing Goodall as an absolute giant whose leadership continued until her final day. The festival's eighth edition, titled 'The Search for Truth,' features discussions on combating disinformation in the age of social media. Both guests argue that algorithms prioritizing engagement over facts create a post-truth environment where negative emotions dominate public discourse. They suggest that regulating tech companies and improving education are necessary steps to counteract the spread of misinformation. Figueres noted that humans are evolutionarily drawn to bad news, but society must consciously choose to surround itself with accurate information rather than fear-based content.
items.title: Christiana Figueres receives inaugural Jane Goodall Earth Medal at Starmus Festival

Zelenskyy stated that the war started by Russia is effectively closing its own skies.
Zelenskyy emphasized that Ukraine does not threaten civilian aircraft but noted the sheer scale of drones in Russian airspace.
This warning follows a week of sustained Russian attacks on Kyiv using jet-powered drones and missiles.

Zelenskyy emphasized that Ukraine does not threaten civilian aircraft but noted the sheer scale of drones in Russian airspace. items.title: Zelenskyy warns Russian airspace will effectively close due to drone operations

key_points: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial deadlocked after four days of deliberations, but Judge William Sullivan asked them to continue.
Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder for killing her three children in January 2023 in Massachusetts.
Her defense argues she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and unable to distinguish right from wrong at the time.
If convicted of first-degree murder, Clancy would face a mandatory life sentence without the possibility of parole.
If found not guilty by reason of insanity, she would be sent to a psychiatric hospital for periodic review.
items.summary: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial reached a deadlock after four days of deliberations, prompting Judge William Sullivan to ask them to keep trying. Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder for killing her three children in Massachusetts in 2023. Her lawyer argues she suffered from postpartum psychosis and could not distinguish right from wrong. The jury, consisting of nine women and three men, has heard weeks of testimony. If found guilty, Clancy could face a mandatory life sentence without parole. Alternatively, she could be found not guilty by reason of insanity and sent to a psychiatric hospital.
items.title: Jurors deadlocked in Lindsay Clancy murder trial but judge urges continued deliberation

Hamas officials stated the officer was wounded and his wife killed during the raid.
The operation involved an Israeli-allied militia and resulted in multiple civilian deaths.
Palestinian health officials reported four people killed in the initial assault, while separate strikes later killed at least six more individuals.
items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that forces captured Hamas internal security chief Muein al-Arabid during a Tuesday operation. Hamas officials claimed the officer was wounded and his wife killed during the raid. The operation involved an Israeli-allied militia and resulted in multiple civilian deaths. items.title: Netanyahu says Israel captured Hamas security chief in Gaza

Funding covers healthcare, security, humanitarian care, and direct business support.
President Juan Jesús Vivas urged national unity and solidarity for the city.
The announcement occurred on the eve of political demonstrations in Ceuta.

Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo described the measures as a shock response intended to safeguard jobs and support businesses. The funds are divided into healthcare, security, humanitarian care for minors, and direct business support. President Juan Jesús Vivas called for national unity, stating the city would never be abandoned despite the challenges. The announcement coincided with political demonstrations in the city highlighting internal divisions.
items.title: Spain approves 309 million euro aid package for Ceuta amid migrant crisis

The groups allege supporters displayed symbols and banners glorifying Ratko Mladic during matches.
Associations stated Mladic was convicted of genocide and war crimes during the 1992-95 Bosnian war.
FENA news agency reported the complaint was filed Tuesday in Brussels.

items.title: Bosnian associations urge UEFA to sanction FC Borac over war criminal glorification

The three leaders could meet if plans proceed as expected during the November event in Shenzhen.
Ushakov noted that Xi mentioned Trump would attend and Putin would likely be an invitee.
Ushakov also announced plans to meet with Cardinal Matteo Maria Zuppi to discuss Ukraine war humanitarian matters.
items.summary: A Kremlin aide reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed a potential trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump. Yuri Ushakov stated the leaders spoke about this possibility during talks in Bishkek. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is scheduled for November in Shenzhen. Ushakov also mentioned separate discussions regarding humanitarian issues in the Ukraine war.
items.title: Kremlin aide says Putin, Trump, Xi may meet at APEC

key_points: Government figures confirm over 6,000 infections and 2,911 deaths from the Bundibugyo Ebola strain.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres described the outbreak as the fastest-growing epidemic on record.
Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba stated that more than 50,000 vaccine doses have arrived for front-line workers.
Violence and insecurity in eastern DRC have prevented response teams from safely reaching affected communities.
Education Minister Raissa Malu introduced radio-based learning to mitigate school disruptions caused by the outbreak.
items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo government reports that confirmed Ebola infections have surpassed 6,000, with 2,911 deaths recorded so far. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated the epidemic is the fastest-growing on record and warned that international resources are lagging behind the reality on the ground. Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba announced a vaccination campaign for over 50,000 front-line workers using doses originally developed for a different variant. Conflict and insecurity in eastern provinces continue to obstruct response teams, who reported attacks while handling Ebola-related deaths. Education Minister Raissa Malu proposed radio-based learning to maintain schooling, though teachers note a lack of necessary infrastructure. Despite these challenges, authorities highlight that more than 1,360 people have recovered from the virus.
items.title: Congo Ebola cases exceed 6,000 as violence hampers response

key_points: El Ciervo Encantado announced it will no longer be based at its state-regulated headquarters in Vedado.
The group stated it will continue creating and presenting art in alternative locations despite institutional pressure.
Founded by Nelda Castillo, the ensemble has operated for thirty years as a critical voice in Cuban theater.
The theater group's decision represents a continued defiance against censorship and bureaucratic control over artistic expression.
items.summary: Cuban theater group El Ciervo Encantado announced it will no longer operate under state supervision after more than a decade of conflicts with the Ministry of Culture. The group stated on social media that it would cease using its Vedado headquarters while continuing to create art in alternative spaces. Founded by Nelda Castillo thirty years ago, the ensemble has long challenged institutional control over Cuban performance art. Their recent decision marks a significant political gesture against censorship and bureaucratic oversight in the country. The group plans to present works in private homes and other venues to maintain their critical voice. This move highlights ongoing tensions between independent artists and state regulators in Cuba's cultural sector.
items.title: Cuban theater group El Ciervo Encantado defies censorship by leaving state headquarters

The article attributes this development to changing climate conditions in the region.
The text mentions potential impacts on global trade and navigation.

The German government announced new sanctions in response to the incident.
Officials stated the attack was a deliberate act by Russian forces.
items.summary: Germany blames Russia for a drone incident at an airport and has announced new sanctions against the country. The German government stated that the attack was a deliberate act by Russian forces. Officials said the measures target individuals and entities linked to the aggression.
items.title: Germany blames Russia for drone incident and imposes sanctions

key_points: Tunisia's President Kais Saied hosted German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul in Tunis on Monday.
Saied called for the European Union to update its relationship with Tunisia to make it more balanced and fair.
Wadephul stated that international cooperation is more important than ever due to global upheaval and crises.
The two nations signed financing agreements of almost 100 million euros and pledged to expand cooperation in energy, water, and digital sectors.
items.summary: Tunisia's President Kais Saied hosted German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul in Tunis to discuss strengthening bilateral relations. Saied urged the European Union to update its partnership with Tunisia, describing it as needing to be more balanced and fair. Wadephul emphasized the importance of international cooperation during global crises while reaffirming Germany and the EU as reliable partners. The two nations signed financing agreements totaling nearly 100 million euros and pledged to expand cooperation in energy transition, water management, and digitalisation.
items.title: Tunisia President Saied calls for balanced EU ties during German visit

key_points: Bangladesh has not received an invitation to join the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement.
Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman said the government views the pact positively but membership depends on current members' intentions.
Analysts warn joining could complicate relations with India and limit Bangladesh's geopolitical options.
Experts argue there is no direct geographical rationale for Bangladesh to participate in a Middle East-focused security arrangement.
items.summary: Bangladesh has not received an invitation to join the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman stated the government views the pact positively but membership depends on the intentions of current members. Analysts note the agreement could complicate Bangladesh's relations with India, a key ally that has recently seen strained ties with Dhaka. Experts warn that joining might limit Bangladesh's geopolitical options and create diplomatic pressures if a conflict arises between India and Pakistan. While some see potential benefits in modernizing defense capabilities, others argue there is no direct geographical rationale for Bangladesh to participate in a Middle East-focused security arrangement.
items.title: Bangladesh has not received an invitation to join the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defense pact

items.title: Former prosecutor urges Osaka office reform after rape accusation

key_points: Scientist Akiko Takii captured a young Asiatic black bear after a sensor alert in Nagano Prefecture.
Researchers collected biological samples from the 15-kilogram bear before releasing it.
The capture happened as nationwide bear attacks have increased, resulting in thousands of culls.
The young bear was too small to receive a GPS tracker during the operation.
items.summary: In Nagano Prefecture, scientist Akiko Takii responded to a sensor alert by capturing a young Asiatic black bear. Researchers collected blood and fur samples from the 15-kilogram animal before releasing it. The capture occurred amid rising nationwide bear attacks that have led to thousands of culls. The bear was too small for a GPS tracker, so it was not tagged.
items.title: Japanese scientist captures young bear to study rising attacks

key_points: SCO member states, including India, condemned military strikes on Iran that caused civilian casualties and economic damage.
The bloc called for resolving the conflict through political and diplomatic means rather than military action.
India expressed condolences for the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei at the summit.

items.summary: The SCO reiterated its condemnation of military strikes on Iran, with India joining other member states in expressing concern over civilian casualties and economic damage. The bloc called for a political resolution to the conflict while condemning terrorism and opposing unilateral coercive measures. India also expressed condolences for the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to discuss expanding ties between the two nations.
items.title: India joins SCO in condemning strikes on Iran and calling for diplomatic resolution

key_points: An IndiGo flight with 229 passengers returned to Goa after an engine failure.
IndiGo stated a technical issue was detected shortly after takeoff.
Air Traffic Control declared a full emergency around 9:30 a.m.
The aircraft is currently undergoing maintenance checks before resuming operations.
items.summary: An IndiGo flight carrying 229 passengers made an emergency landing in Goa after one engine failed shortly after takeoff. IndiGo reported that a technical issue was detected and pilots followed standard procedures to return safely. Air Traffic Control declared a full emergency before the aircraft landed at Manohar International Airport. The airline stated the plane is undergoing maintenance checks and passengers have been arranged for transport to their destination.
items.title: IndiGo flight returns to Goa after engine failure

The officer, who served 10.5 years, had confessed to being gay and disclosed his relationship with a foreigner during a compassionate discharge application.
An inquiry found him guilty of breaching discipline and travelling abroad without permission.
The bench ruled that changing the order prevents lasting career stigma while noting the effect of dismissal and discharge is identical in this context.
items.summary: The Armed Forces Tribunal principal bench converted the dismissal of a non-commissioned Indian Air Force officer into a routine discharge. The officer, who served 10.5 years, had confessed to being gay and disclosed his relationship with a foreigner during a compassionate discharge application. An inquiry found him guilty of breaching discipline and travelling abroad without permission. The bench ruled that changing the order prevents lasting career stigma while noting the effect of dismissal and discharge is identical in this context.
items.title: Armed Forces Tribunal changes gay ex-IAF officer dismissal to routine discharge

key_points: S&P Global is discussing a potential spinout of Capital IQ Pro, though a transaction is not guaranteed.
People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that one option is listing the business separately with a high single-digit billion valuation.
S&P Global shares rose as much as 6.3% after investors welcomed the possibility of the separation.
A standalone CapIQ would compete with established providers like FactSet Research Systems and the London Stock Exchange Group's data arm.
items.summary: S&P Global is exploring a potential spinout of Capital IQ Pro, a business unit within its Market Intelligence division. People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that discussions are preliminary and may not lead to a transaction. One option involves listing the business separately with a valuation in the high single-digit billions. Investors welcomed the possibility, causing S&P Global shares to rise as much as 6.3%. The move would allow CapIQ to compete directly with providers like FactSet Research Systems.
items.title: S&P Global considers multibillion-dollar spinout of Capital IQ Pro

key_points: Tata Motors received European Central Bank approval for its 3.8 billion euro takeover offer for Iveco Group.
The company confirmed that all prior sector regulatory authorizations required for the voluntary total takeover offer have been obtained.
Italy's Consob is currently reviewing the offer document before it can be published to shareholders.
The acquisition aims to substantially expand Tata Motors' commercial vehicle presence in Europe and other developed markets.
items.summary: Tata Motors secured European Central Bank approval for its proposed acquisition of Iveco Group, valued at approximately 40,000 crore rupees. The company confirmed that all prior sector regulatory authorizations have been obtained, keeping the deal on schedule for an August completion. While British and Spanish regulators have already cleared the transaction, Italy's Consob remains the final regulatory hurdle before the offer document is published. Once approved, the deal will expand Tata's commercial vehicle footprint significantly across European and other developed markets.
items.title: Tata Motors receives ECB approval for 40,000 crore Iveco takeover

key_points: SB Energy filed for an IPO with the SEC, targeting a listing on Nasdaq under ticker SBE.
The company plans to raise between $5 billion and $7 billion to expand its AI data centre business.
Chief executive Rich Hossfeld noted that Nvidia's participation strengthens the company's ability to secure investment-grade financing.
SB Energy reported a net loss of approximately $3.2 billion in the first half of 2026, with no revenue from AI data centres.
The filing states the company is substantially dependent on OpenAI as both a tenant and equity investor.
items.summary: SB Energy has filed for an initial public offering with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, aiming to list on Nasdaq under ticker SBE. The company, backed by SoftBank, OpenAI, and Nvidia, plans to raise between $5 billion and $7 billion to fund its AI infrastructure expansion. Chief executive Rich Hossfeld stated that Nvidia's involvement helps unlock investment-grade financing for the project. SB Energy reported a net loss of approximately $3.2 billion in the first half of 2026, with no operational AI data centres yet. The filing highlights the company's substantial dependence on OpenAI as both a tenant and equity investor. Investors will monitor how public markets value the company as it navigates potential regulatory and community challenges associated with rapid data centre construction.
items.title: SB Energy files for IPO after Nvidia backs OpenAI data centre project

key_points: Police said six pilgrims died and 14 were injured in a crash on the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal Expressway.
The victims were returning from Rajasthan after visiting the Khatu Shyam Temple.
Police suspect the driver fell asleep before the collision and have fled the scene.
Deputy Commissioner Jayendra Singh Chhillar ordered a nearby liquor vend sealed after finding irregularities.
items.summary: Police said six pilgrims died and 14 were injured after a pick-up crashed into a stationary truck on the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal Expressway in Haryana. The victims were returning from Rajasthan after visiting the Khatu Shyam Temple. Police suspect the driver fell asleep before the collision and have fled the scene. Deputy Commissioner Jayendra Singh Chhillar inspected a nearby liquor vend, found irregularities, and ordered it sealed. He stated that disregard for road safety rules would not be tolerated.
items.title: Six pilgrims killed after pick-up crashes into truck on Haryana expressway

key_points: Four batsmen scored centuries during the opening day of the Senior Men's Multi-Day Super League.
Aditya Vardhan achieved an unbeaten double century of 202 in the Under-19 selection matches.
Mayur Shetty Kumar took five wickets for 10 runs, joining four other bowlers with five-wicket hauls.
Vaibhav Agarwal scored an unbeaten 126 from 74 balls in the 'C' Division league match.

items.title: Four Centuries and Five-Wicket Hauls Mark Day One of Hyderabad Cricket League

Anandi Devi Nimbalkar and her son Omraje Nimbalkar filed the petition challenging the sessions court's decision.
A division bench of Justices Ajey Gadkari and Kamal Khata directed the Maharashtra government and accused to file their responses.
The sessions court had acquitted the accused citing a flawed investigation and unreliable approver testimony.

key_points: The Bombay High Court ordered the BMC to examine its land holdings for constructing free housing for sanitation workers.
A bench voiced sharp displeasure regarding an 18-year delay in implementing a 2008 government policy for municipal staff.
The court rejected a recent affidavit from the Municipal Commissioner as vague and non-compliant with previous judicial directions.
The Municipal Commissioner must file a comprehensive report by September 9, 2026, detailing municipal property occupancy and feasibility.
items.summary: The Bombay High Court directed the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation to audit its land holdings for free housing for sanitation workers. A bench expressed displeasure over an 18-year delay in implementing a 2008 policy granting ownership homes to staff. The court rejected a vague affidavit from the Municipal Commissioner and questioned the administration's neglect of essential workforce members. Officials must submit a fresh report by September 9, 2026, or face an independent committee inspection.

key_points: The Vision Theatre reopened in 2026 after a 15-year, nearly $40 million restoration led by the City of Los Angeles.
The project repaired structural vulnerabilities and restored historic features while upgrading mechanical systems and accessibility.
The 729-seat venue will be managed by the city's Cultural Affairs Department to serve as a neighborhood arts hub.
Officials describe the reopening as a statement of value for historic theatres in South Los Angeles communities.
items.summary: The Vision Theatre in South Los Angeles reopened in 2026 following a 15-year restoration project costing nearly $40 million. The City of Los Angeles initiated the effort in 2011 to preserve the historic landmark and revitalize the Leimert Park Cultural and Arts District. Work included structural repairs, system upgrades, and the restoration of original architectural features while ensuring modern accessibility. The 729-seat venue is now managed by the city's Cultural Affairs Department to host diverse performances and community events. Officials state the project signals a commitment to preserving cultural spaces in predominantly Black and Latino neighborhoods. The theatre aims to provide economic benefits to the village while remaining accessible to local residents through targeted programming.
items.title: Los Angeles reopens restored Vision Theatre after 15 years

Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine does not threaten civilian aviation but the scale of drone presence must be taken into account.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine could temporarily clear drones from Russian skies to support diplomatic efforts.

At least 12 people were killed in Kyiv during recent Russian strikes. Zelenskyy added that Ukraine might temporarily clear drones from specific areas to aid diplomatic negotiations.
items.title: Zelenskyy warns airlines Russian airspace is unsafe due to drones

The raid at his residence in Panayappilly uncovered 42 bottles totaling 21 litres of suspected IMFL.
Libin Jose P.A. was booked under Section 55 of the Kerala Abkari Act for illegal possession.

Authorities booked him under Section 55 of the Kerala Abkari Act for illegal storage and possession of liquor beyond permissible limits.
items.title: Police Arrest Man in Kochi for Storing 21 Litres of Suspected IMFL

The manufacturing sector grew 9.2%, supported by tax cuts and interest rate reductions.
Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran cautioned that Hormuz instability could sustain high oil prices.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed for local purchases to reduce trade deficits.
Rising inflation and a poor monsoon may weaken rural consumption in coming quarters.

key_points: The Telangana High Court stayed a single judge's order that halted the Kalyana Lakshmi and Shaadi Mubarak schemes.
The bench allowed the state government to continue disbursing financial assistance to brides' families across all communities.
The court directed the health department to file an affidavit on actions taken against the sale of MTP kits without prescriptions.
Bailable warrants were issued against two principal secretaries for failing to appear in a contempt case regarding compensation delays.
items.summary: A Telangana High Court division bench stayed interim orders halting the Kalyana Lakshmi and Shaadi Mubarak schemes, allowing financial assistance to continue. The bench noted the Comptroller and Auditor-General had not indicted the expenditure as lacking legislative sanction. In a separate matter, the court directed the health department to detail actions taken regarding the unregulated sale of abortion kits. Additionally, the court issued bailable warrants against two principal secretaries for failing to appear in a contempt case concerning delayed compensation payments. The court emphasized that government officers cannot authorize others to represent them in contempt proceedings.
items.title: Telangana HC Stays Stay Orders on Welfare Schemes and Issues Warrants

key_points: The SEC submitted a proposal to the White House Office of Management and Budget to expand retail access to private markets.
SEC Chairman Paul Atkins stated that market exposure should not be reserved for wealthy insiders.
The plan would amend existing acts to allow performance fees for a wider client base.
Critics like Better Markets warn that private investments offer fewer disclosures than public ones.
items.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission submitted a proposal to the White House Office of Management and Budget to broaden retail investor access to private markets. SEC Chairman Paul Atkins stated that market exposure should not be reserved for wealthy insiders. The plan would amend existing acts to allow performance fees for a wider client base. items.title: SEC Plans to Expand Retail Access to Private Markets

items.title: Blackstone sells entire EPL stake for 2032 crore to funds and insurers

key_points: Russia controls about a fifth of Ukraine's territory and continues advancing toward Donbas cities while intensifying attacks on infrastructure.
Negotiating positions remain far apart, with Russia demanding recognition of territorial gains before a ceasefire and Ukraine seeking a ceasefire first.
Russia sustains the conflict through a wartime economy and high domestic support, while Ukraine faces manpower shortages and dependency on Western aid.
The EU is expanding defense spending, and China is deepening trade with Russia, though a full Sino-Russian alliance is not attractive.
India must preserve strategic autonomy by maintaining partnerships with the US, Russia, and Europe while the conflict reshapes global security.
items.summary: The article analyzes the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, noting that peace remains distant due to divergent negotiating positions and mutual distrust. Russia controls roughly a fifth of Ukraine's territory and continues steady advances toward Donbas fortress cities while intensifying aerial attacks on critical infrastructure. Ukraine faces manpower shortages and relies heavily on Western support, having suffered a collapsed counter-offensive in 2023. Diplomatic efforts, including the Anchorage formula requiring Ukrainian recognition of Russian control over five regions, have failed to bridge the gap. Russia insists on addressing territorial and political questions before any ceasefire, whereas Ukraine seeks a ceasefire as a first step. The conflict has hardened into a test of endurance, with Russia sustaining operations through a wartime economy and high domestic support. External dimensions involve the EU expanding defense spending and China deepening trade with Russia in yuan and roubles. For India, the crisis impacts energy security and strategic autonomy, necessitating careful navigation between Moscow, Washington, and Brussels. The author concludes that a prolonged conflict punctuated by intermittent talks is the most likely trajectory, leaving Europe with higher defense spending and a militarized eastern frontier.
items.title: Ukraine conflict shows no end in sight as Russia advances and diplomacy stalls

Justice Sachin Datta awarded over Rs 10 lakh to a chartered accountant who faced professional disadvantage upon returning from leave.
The court ruled that retaining salary while stripping responsibilities violates the Maternity Benefit Act and Article 14.
The court directed the Centre to frame rules ensuring effective implementation of maternity protections.

It directed the Centre to frame rules ensuring effective implementation of maternity protections.

key_points: Four people, including three family members, died in separate landslides in Guwahati on Tuesday.
The Assam State Disaster Management Authority identified the deceased in the Mathgharia incident as Nagen Rajbongshi, his wife, and their daughter.
A 65-year-old woman died in a separate landslide at Satgaon amid incessant rainfall.
Five people were injured in landslide incidents across Assam, with rescue operations ongoing.
items.summary: Officials report four deaths in two separate landslides in Guwahati, Assam, on Tuesday. The Assam State Disaster Management Authority confirmed three family members died in Nizarapar while a 65-year-old woman died in Satgaon. Incessant rainfall caused the incidents, injuring five others across the state. Rescue teams recovered the bodies and continue relief operations in affected areas.
items.title: Four people killed in Guwahati landslides triggered by heavy rainfall

key_points: Starman Optical agreed to purchase a 90% stake in GoPro for $285 million in cash.
The acquisition targets GoPro's debt, rising component costs, and intense competition from Chinese manufacturers.
Starman intends to utilize GoPro's extensive patent portfolio to enter commercial, defense, and AI sectors.
GoPro shares increased by over 50% following the news, trading near $1.33 per share.
The deal is projected to close by the end of 2026, with GoPro remaining publicly listed.
items.summary: Starman Optical has agreed to acquire a 90% stake in GoPro for $285 million in cash to help the camera maker address financial challenges. The deal aims to alleviate GoPro's debt, rising memory chip costs, and competition from Chinese rivals like DJI and Insta360. Starman, a US optical parts manufacturer, plans to leverage GoPro's 2,500 patents to expand into commercial, defense, and AI data center markets. GoPro shares rose more than 50% after the announcement, trading at approximately $1.33, though the offer price of $1.14 per share remains below the current market value. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026, allowing GoPro to retain its consumer business while pursuing new technological opportunities.
items.title: Starman Optical buys 90% of GoPro for $285 million to address debt and competition

key_points: The government reintroduced an export duty of ₹1.5 per litre on petrol.
Diesel export duties remain unchanged at ₹24 per litre, excluding the cess.
The export levy on aviation turbine fuel was reduced by 50 paise to ₹19 per litre.
Excise duties for domestic consumption remain unaffected by these changes.

items.title: Government reintroduces petrol export duty at 1.5 rupees per litre

Modi stated that the fight against terrorism requires dismantling the entire ecosystem of financing and radicalization without double standards.
The Bishkek Declaration condemned military strikes on Iran and supported a diplomatic settlement for the Palestinian question.
SCO leaders adopted new initiatives covering drug control, biodiversity conservation, and artificial intelligence development through 2030.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, calling for dialogue to resolve the West Asia conflict rather than military action. He stated that terrorism remains a serious global challenge requiring a unified approach to dismantle financing and recruitment networks. While not naming specific countries, his remarks on using terrorism as a policy instrument appeared directed at Pakistan. The summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration, which condemned military strikes on Iran and emphasized resolving the Palestinian question through political means. Leaders also approved initiatives on drug control, biodiversity conservation, and artificial intelligence development for the coming decade.
items.title: Modi urges West Asia diplomacy and targets terror ecosystem at SCO summit

Muslims accounted for 40.7% of all deletions, though the report could not determine if they were removed at a higher rate due to missing data.
The institute noted that in two constituencies, deleted electors exceeded votes cast.

The Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.1% as technology stocks came under pressure from higher borrowing costs.

Oil prices climbed above $88 a barrel as Middle East tensions fueled inflation fears.
President Donald Trump threatened a strong response to Iran after recent attacks on US military bases.
items.summary: US stocks declined on Tuesday as investors worried about rising oil prices, higher bond yields, and potential Federal Reserve interest rate changes. Goldman Sachs traders noted market nervousness, while Capital Markets analysts expect AI to remain a dominant market driver despite concerns about China's AI progress. Akamai Technologies received an analyst upgrade, and Hut 8 shares rose in premarket trading following reports of a new data center development.
items.title: US stocks fall as oil prices and bond yields rise ahead of Fed meeting
